I want to clarify that I'm an atheist and would take an astrophysicist's opinion on such matters over that of a backwoods preacher, any day of the week. However, I do live in the bible belt and this question occurred to me. In another recent thread, we'd been discussing expansion, and the observed data indicates that there was no center to the big bang, everything is "moving" away from everything else, quotation marks because it's space itself that seems to be expanding. I hope I didn't articulate that too, too badly. But wouldn't it look that way if Earth were at the center of the explosion? An ant on the proverbial balloon would see all other ants moving away from him and each other - but he'd also see that on a flat surface in which they were scattered away by, say, a firecracker. What would I say to a creationist, if this came up?
Could a creationist reasonably interpret universal expansion as compatible with an earth-centric universe?

Well, either there's no center or everything is at the center. The more tradition analogy is to think of a balloon that starts out microscopic, every point on the balloon's surface was at the center before it inflated.

But those observations don't work unless the universe is really ~13 billion years old.

There are a hundred different kinds of creationists.

To make your hobby of arguing with them more fun, pick one who does Plasma Cosmology.

The universe very clearly looks like the Earth (or rather, the Solar system/Milky Way) is at the center of it. But it does so in a way that every other point in the universe looks equally much like the center of the universe. It's called the cosmological principle. If you start from the cosmological principle, you can prove that Hubble expansion (the one which we see) is the only kind of expansion the universe can have, because every point will seem like the center that the rest of the universe is receding away from.

Elderly Man Smokes Pipe As Car Sinks

An elderly man who accidentally drove into a lake sat in his car calmly smoking his pipe as he waited to be rescued, emergency services have said.

Crews were called to a farm in Loxley, Warwickshire, at about 14:50 BST on Tuesday.

The man, in his eighties, had gone there to fish.

West Midlands Ambulance Service said: "He smoked his pipe and chatted to the farmer, who went into the lake in waders".

Firefighters carried the driver from his car back onto land.

"He wasn't hurt or even cold but crews removed his clothing to ensure he didn't get cold and he was driven home in the ambulance," a spokesman said.
